<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-author">Author</button></h2><div id="work-acc-author" class="accordion-collapse collapse show"><div class="accordion-body"><p class="mb-0 work-author"><a href="../poets/rajanaka-ruyyaka.html">Rājānaka Ruyyaka</a></p></div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Sāhityamīmāṃsā is a treatise on poetics and literary theory written by Rājānaka Ruyyaka. The work is divided into 12 chapters, each dealing with different aspects of literature, such as the nature of poetry, the classification of poetry, figures of speech, and the role of emotion in poetry. The treatise is highly regarded for its clear and concise style, as well as its systematic approach to literary analysis. It has been studied and commented upon by many scholars of Sanskrit literature over the centuries.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Sāhityamīmāṃsā has 12 chapters. The chapters are as follows:<br>1. Pūrva pakṣa: Critique of other literary theories<br>2. Siddhānta: Ruyyaka’s own literary theory<br>3. Vākya: Sentence-level analysis of literary meaning<br>4. Pada: Word-level analysis of literary meaning<br>5. Artha: Analysis of literary meaning in relation to context<br>6. Abhidhāna: Analysis of literary vocabulary and terminology<br>7. Alaṅkāra: Analysis of literary figures of speech<br>8. Upamā: Analysis of simile and metaphor in literature<br>9. Atīndriya: Analysis of the use of the supernatural in literature<br>10. Anumāna: Analysis of literary inference and suggestion<br>11. Samarthana: Analysis of the structure and organization of literary works<br>12. Nirṇaya: Conclusion and summary of Ruyyaka’s literary theory.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Sāhityamīmāṃsā&quot; is a unique work in Sanskrit literature as it focuses on the examination of the principles of literary criticism and aesthetics. Unlike other works that primarily focus on the technical aspects of poetry, this work emphasizes the study of literary theory and the philosophy of art. The author, Rājānaka Ruyyaka, presents a comprehensive analysis of the nature of poetry, the role of the poet, and the relationship between the poet and the audience. He also explores the concept of beauty and how it is expressed through various literary devices.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Sāhityamīmāṃsā by Rājānaka Ruyyaka is an important work in the field of Sanskrit poetics and literary criticism. The text presents a comprehensive analysis of the nature of literature and its various aspects, including language, style, and meaning. It also discusses the role of the poet and the audience in the creation and interpretation of literature. The work has made significant contributions to the development of Sanskrit literary theory, particularly in the area of poetics. It has influenced many subsequent scholars in the field, and its insights and ideas have been incorporated into later works on literary criticism.<br><br>One notable aspect of Sāhityamīmāṃsā is that it includes a discussion on the concept of rasa, which is considered to be one of the most important concepts in Sanskrit poetics. Rasa refers to the emotional experience or flavour that is evoked in the audience when they experience a work of literature. Ruyyaka provides a detailed analysis of rasa and its various types, as well as the means by which it is created in literature. His ideas on rasa have had a significant impact on subsequent Sanskrit literary theory, and his work is still studied and referenced by scholars today. Additionally, Sāhityamīmāṃsā is also notable for its clear and concise writing style, which has made it accessible to a wide range of readers and has helped to popularize the study of Sanskrit poetics.</div></div></div>
